title: Erdős #401: Factorial Divisibility with Prime Products

problemStatement.formal: ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto f atTop atTop ∧ ∀ r, ∃ᶠ n in atTop, ∃ a₁ a₂, a₁! * a₂! ∣ n! * primorialPow(r,n) ∧ a₁ + a₂ > n + f(r) * log(n)
problemStatement.plain: Does there exist f(r) → ∞ such that for infinitely many n, there exist a₁, a₂ with a₁ + a₂ > n + f(r)·log(n) where a₁!·a₂! | n!·2ⁿ·3ⁿ·...·pᵣⁿ? Answer: YES (Barreto-Leeham 2026). The 'for all large n' version is FALSE (Sothanaphan).
whyMatters: Shows prime power factors allow exceeding classical O(log n) bounds
Complete resolution: YES for infinitely many n, NO for all large n

proven: FactorialDivides: symmetry, monotonicity in r, zero cases
erdos_401_complete: conjunction of YES and NOT-strong
